snippet.title: Testing the new Slim-G Antenna! SOTA Activation on Easington Fell
snippet.description:
​Heading out for a quick mission to bag another 1-pointer! In this video, I’m activating Easington Fell (G/SP-012) in the Southern Pennines / Forest of Bowland area. 

​The main objective for today's trip is putting my new setup through its paces—rigging up the portable mast alongside the Slim-G antenna to see how well it performs out in the field.

Easington Fell offers brilliant VHF take-off and lovely views, making it an ideal spot to test new gear and rack up those SOTA points.

​Let's see how the new antenna handles the breeze and how many chasers we can pull in!

​Summit Info:
​Summit: Easington Fell, UK  
​SOTA Reference: G/SP-012  
​Points: 1  
​Elevation: 396m (1,299 ft)

snippet.title: Rookie Ham Broke State Record
snippet.description:
How does someone go from brand new ham to more than 17,000 contacts in just six months? In this interview, I sit down with Brandon, W4SFD, who has been licensed for less than a year and has already become one of the most active Parks on the Air (POTA) operators around.
Brandon tells how it all started: he watched a few POTA videos on YouTube and decided to try an activation himself. That first activation was only six months ago, and he hasn’t slowed down since. We talk about what kept him going, how he built his contact count so quickly, and what he’s learned that can help other new hams get on the air.
We also get into his gear. Brandon explains why the Yaesu FT-891 is his favorite POTA radio and walks through several of the antennas he uses in the field. If you’re putting together a portable HF station for POTA, his real-world experience will help you see what works.
Then there’s the big story: Brandon set a new state record during the Tennessee QSO Party this year. He shares how the day went, what his strategy was, and what it felt like to set a record in his first year as a ham.
Whether you’re a new ham thinking about your first POTA activation, a seasoned activator looking for ideas, or someone interested in contesting and QSO parties, Brandon’s story shows how far you can go in a short time with the right mix of curiosity and time on the air.

snippet.title: Maduro Captured. 41 Days Later, a License Named Chevron.
snippet.description:
Over 150 aircraft. One captured president. 41 days later, a Treasury license naming Chevron. Here are the dates, from Chevron's $2M inaugural gift to the capture operation and the license that followed. Timing is not proof.

Follow-up to our Chevron & Venezuela Short: this one walks through the operation itself.

THE TIMELINE (days counted from the Jan 3, 2026 capture)
• Dec 13, 2024 (day −386): Chevron Products Company gave $2,000,000 to the Trump Vance Inaugural Committee (FEC Form 13, Schedule 13-A, p.57). That was an inaugural donation, not campaign or PAC money.
• Aug 7, 2025 (day −149): The State and Justice Departments raised the reward for information leading to Maduro's arrest or conviction to up to $50M. It had been $25M since Jan 10, 2025.
• Sep 2, 2025 (day −123): The first U.S. strike on an alleged drug boat from Venezuela. The strikes were later run under Operation Southern Spear. Their legality is disputed.
• Nov 16, 2025 (day −48): The USS Gerald R. Ford carrier strike group entered the Caribbean Sea (SOUTHCOM).
• Dec 10, 2025 (day −24): U.S. forces seized the sanctioned oil tanker Skipper off Venezuela. Caracas called it "piracy."
• Jan 3, 2026 (day 0), early Jan 3 Caracas time (DoD: Jan 2 U.S. time): Operation Absolute Resolve. The Pentagon says more than 150 aircraft were involved. U.S. forces captured Nicolás Maduro and Cilia Flores in Caracas.
• Jan 5, 2026: Both pleaded not guilty in Manhattan federal court. The charges are allegations.
• Feb 13, 2026 (day +41): OFAC General License 50 authorized oil and gas operations in Venezuela for BP, Chevron, Eni, Repsol and Shell. GL 50A (Feb 18) added Maurel & Prom.
• Sep 2, 2026 (day +242): Chevron's joint ventures announced plans to invest over $7B over five years. That's a plan, not money already spent.

Timing is not proof. This shows events in order. It does not show that any license, deal or military action was bought or caused by a donation. European rivals got the same license. A Chevron spokesperson told Reuters (Jan 2026) the company operates in compliance with all laws, regulations and sanctions frameworks. Chevron has been in Venezuela since 1923.

SOUTHCOM, Ford enters Caribbean (Nov 16, 2025): https://www.southcom.mil/MEDIA/NEWS-ARTICLES/Article/4332637/gerald-r-ford-carrier-strike-group-enters-caribbean-sea/
Reuters, tanker seized (Dec 10, 2025): https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/trump-administration-seizes-oil-tanker-off-venezuela-coast-us-officials-say-2025-12-10/
U.S. Dept. of War, capture of Maduro (Jan 3, 2026): https://www.war.gov/News/News-Stories/Article/Article/4370431/trump-announces-us-militarys-capture-of-maduro/
Reuters, not-guilty plea (Jan 5, 2026): https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/venezuelas-maduro-appear-us-court-trump-says-further-strikes-possible-2026-01-05/

Reuters via Yahoo Finance (Jan 14, 2026), Chevron compliance statement: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/exclusive-chevron-expected-receive-expanded-204348786.html

snippet.title: Les SMS des avions.
snippet.description:
L'ACARS (Aircraft Communications, Addressing and Reporting System) est une liaison de données utilisée depuis 1978 pour échanger de courts messages entre l'avion et le sol. Elle passe par radio VHF au-dessus des terres, puis par satellite ou par radio HF au-dessus des océans et près des pôles. Les messages signalent les étapes du vol, apportent météo et mises à jour du plan de vol, et transmettent des données sur l'état des moteurs, parfois automatiquement. Au-dessus des océans, certaines autorisations du contrôle aérien arrivent aussi par écrit, grâce au système FANS.

Sources :
SKYbrary – Aircraft Communications, Addressing and Reporting System

FAA – AC 20-140B, Guidelines for Design Approval of Aircraft Data Link Communication Systems

Rolls-Royce – Engine Health Monitoring (EHM)

snippet.title: Chevron Gave $2M. Lost Its Venezuela License. Now: 2x the Oil.
snippet.description:
Chevron lobbied on Venezuela every quarter for ten years. In December 2024 it gave $2 million to Trump's inauguration. Then it lost its Venezuela license. Here's the dated timeline of how it ended up with plans to double its oil there.

Gift made by Chevron Products Company to the Trump-Vance Inaugural Committee (FEC Form 13).

THE TIMELINE
• Dec 13, 2024: Chevron Products Company gave $2,000,000 to the Trump Vance Inaugural Committee (FEC Form 13). Chevron says it supports the inaugural committees of both parties.
• Feb 26, 2025: Trump announced he was reversing the Biden-era Venezuela oil "concessions," meaning Chevron's license.
• Mar 4, 2025: Treasury (OFAC General License 41A) ordered a wind-down by Apr 3, 2025.
• 2016–2025: Every quarterly lobbying report Chevron U.S.A. filed lists Venezuela issues ("Venezuela Sanctions" / "Venezuela Energy Issues"). That's 40 of 40 quarters. In 2025 it reported $7.96M in federal lobbying across all issues, not just Venezuela.
• Late July 2025: Chevron got a restricted license back, with no cash allowed to go to Maduro's government (Reuters, Jul 30, 2025; also reported by The Washington Post, Jul 24, 2025).
• Jan 3, 2026: U.S. forces captured Nicolás Maduro.
• Feb 13, 2026: OFAC General License 50 authorized oil and gas operations in Venezuela for Chevron, BP, Shell, Eni and Repsol. GL 50A replaced it on Feb 18 and added Maurel & Prom.
• Apr 13, 2026: In an asset swap with PDVSA, Chevron's stake in the Petroindependencia joint venture rose to 49%.
• Sep 2, 2026: Chevron's joint ventures announced plans to invest over $7B over five years and more than double output, to about 600,000 barrels a day. That's a plan, not current output.
Timing is not proof. This timeline shows events in order. It does not show that any license or deal was bought. A Chevron spokesperson told Reuters in January 2026 that the company operates in compliance with all laws, regulations and sanctions frameworks. Chevron has been in Venezuela since 1923. Associated Press (Sep 2, 2026) described Chevron as the only U.S. oil company with a major presence in Venezuela.

Chevron lobbied on Venezuela every quarter for ten years. In December 2024 it gave $2 million to Trump's inauguration. Then it lost its Venezuela license. Here's the dated timeline of how it ended up with plans to double its oil there.

Gift made by Chevron Products Company to the Trump-Vance Inaugural Committee (FEC Form 13).

THE TIMELINE
• Dec 13, 2024: Chevron Products Company gave $2,000,000 to the Trump Vance Inaugural Committee (FEC Form 13). Chevron says it supports the inaugural committees of both parties.
• Feb 26, 2025: Trump announced he was reversing the Biden-era Venezuela oil "concessions," meaning Chevron's license.
• Mar 4, 2025: Treasury (OFAC General License 41A) ordered a wind-down by Apr 3, 2025.
• 2016–2025: Every quarterly lobbying report Chevron U.S.A. filed lists Venezuela issues ("Venezuela Sanctions" / "Venezuela Energy Issues"). That's 40 of 40 quarters. In 2025 it reported $7.96M in federal lobbying across all issues, not just Venezuela.
• Late July 2025: Chevron got a restricted license back, with no cash allowed to go to Maduro's government (Reuters, Jul 30, 2025; also reported by The Washington Post, Jul 24, 2025).
• Jan 3, 2026: U.S. forces captured Nicolás Maduro.
• Feb 13, 2026: OFAC General License 50 authorized oil and gas operations in Venezuela for Chevron, BP, Shell, Eni and Repsol. GL 50A replaced it on Feb 18 and added Maurel & Prom.
• Apr 13, 2026: In an asset swap with PDVSA, Chevron's stake in the Petroindependencia joint venture rose to 49%.
• Sep 2, 2026: Chevron's joint ventures announced plans to invest over $7B over five years and more than double output, to about 600,000 barrels a day. That's a plan, not current output.
Timing is not proof. This timeline shows events in order. It does not show that any license or deal was bought. A Chevron spokesperson told Reuters in January 2026 that the company operates in compliance with all laws, regulations and sanctions frameworks. Chevron has been in Venezuela since 1923. Associated Press (Sep 2, 2026) described Chevron as the only U.S. oil company with a major presence in Venezuela.

snippet.description:
Can you really talk to space using an inexpensive handheld ham radio? In this beginner's guide, I'll show you how to track satellites, configure your amateur radio frequencies, and make your very first contact in orbit from your own backyard and connect to a repeater. 

Amateur radio opens up incredible possibilities even if you're just starting out. You don't need a massive antenna tower to hear astronauts or transmit through low-Earth orbit repeaters—just the right setup and timing.

Key Takeaways:

Affordable Gear Setup: How to get started with an entry-level handheld transceiver (HT) and an upgraded antenna.
Finding Satellites & the ISS: How to use mobile pass-tracking apps to pinpoint exact flyover windows and elevation angles.
Frequency & Tone Programming: Step-by-step walkthrough of programming split frequencies, offsets, and CTCSS tones for space repeaters.

Beating the Doppler Shift: How frequency shifts while a satellite moves across the sky and how to compensate on the fly.
Field Tips for Clean Signals: Real-world antenna aiming techniques to lock onto passes and make two-way contact.

snippet.description:
In his Nov 6 interview with 60 Minutes, Trump said he didn't lift diesel sanctions on Russia. On Oct 9, 2026, the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control issued Russia-related General License 135, 'Authorizing Transactions Related to the Sale, Delivery, Offloading, and Importation of Diesel Fuel of Russian Federation Origin.' snippet.title: The End of VARA HF? Why I’m Backing Mercury
snippet.description:
VARA HF, XARA and Project Mercury: what comes next for Winlink and off-grid ham radio? I share my take on the VARA HF and VARA FM compatibility changes, and why we need native software modems on the devices we already carry.

Read the full blog post and supporting background, including the VARA HF 4.9.1 / VARA FM 4.4.1 update and the January 1, 2027 compatibility change:
https://oh8stn.org/blog/2026/11/10/vara-or-open-source-xara-what-do-you-think/

I paid for VARA, I use it, and I’m happy with its performance. Developers have a right to be paid for their work. I also want the freedom to run a capable software modem natively on Linux, Android, iPadOS, macOS, an iPhone or a Raspberry Pi.

For field and off-grid communications, mobility, energy efficiency and the amount of equipment we carry matter. Having to add a Windows computer to support the device we actually want to use is a practical limitation. This is why I’m backing Project Mercury and pushing for native modem support.

In this video, I discuss XARA’s discontinuation, VARA compatibility, Wine and TCP/IP workarounds, and what I want to see from Mercury. That includes modem libraries developers can integrate into native applications, along with proper Mercury support in Winlink Express, Pat Winlink and RadioMail.

The goal is for VARA to become another tool in our toolboxes, with the freedom to choose the modem and operating system that fit the job.

What would Mercury need to offer before you would add it to your field station or RMS gateway? Let me know in the comments.

snippet.title: When Phones Die: Radio 101 for Filipinos in Canada
snippet.description:
When phones die, radio still works.

Your phone just died. The power is out, the Wi-Fi is gone, and the cell network is overloaded. Who do you call? Who tells you what's happening outside? In the movies, there's always one person who picks up a radio — and suddenly, they're not alone anymore.

This is a beginner-friendly guide to radio communication for Filipinos abroad — from a simple family walkie-talkie, all the way to getting your ham licence in Canada. No bunker. No expert knowledge needed to start.

What you'll learn:

• Why phones fail first in a storm or outage, and why radio often keeps working

• The Radio Ladder: listen and charge, family radios, listening to ham radio, getting licensed, and joining a net

• Family radios in Canada: licence-exempt FRS/GMRS handhelds up to 2 watts for short-range family use

• A simple family communication plan you can make tonight: an out-of-area contact, check-in times, a family channel plus a backup, two meeting points, and a power plan

• How to get licensed in Canada: the ISED Amateur Radio Operator Certificate, 100 questions, 70% to pass for Basic, 80% or more for Basic with Honours and HF

• What movies get right — and what they get wrong — about radio in a disaster

One rule to remember: please don't transmit on amateur frequencies until you're licensed, and only use equipment certified for the service you're using in Canada.

Have you ever used a two-way radio? Are you thinking about getting licensed? What country are you watching from? Tell me in the comments.

Subscribe to Pinoy Prepper Central for more affordable, apartment-friendly survival for Filipinos abroad — and for any newcomer starting over in a cold, foreign land. Be ready, stay calm, help each other.

General information only, not legal advice. Radio rules differ by country — always check your local regulator before transmitting. For emergencies in Canada, call 911.

snippet.title: I Activated This Park… Then POTA Removed It!
snippet.description:
I activated this POTA park, made over 300 QSOs, and shortly afterward, POTA removed it from the program! What happened?

Join me for another portable ham radio adventure at the beautiful Village Historique Acadien near Caraquet, New Brunswick, Canada.

This fascinating historical attraction celebrates the rich Acadian heritage of Atlantic Canada, and it turned out to be a fantastic location for amateur radio. With over 300 contacts in the log, the activation was a tremendous success, with plenty of stations eager to make contact with VE9CF.

But there's an unexpected twist to this story!

Shortly after my visit, the Village Historique Acadien was removed from the Parks on the Air (POTA) program.

The removal was carried out by POTA VE9 Mapping Coordinator AB0O, on the same day that 24 other locations were removed during an audit and cleanup of POTA references in New Brunswick and Canada.

Why was this particular historical location removed?

I haven't been given an explanation for its removal, and that's what makes this story particularly interesting. One day it was an eligible POTA location, and shortly afterward, it was gone from the program.

Fortunately, removing a location from POTA doesn't erase the adventure, the contacts, or the wonderful experience of operating portable from such a historic part of New Brunswick.

In this video, you'll experience the activation, hear some of the contacts, and discover why this location has an interesting story beyond the radio contacts themselves.

Thanks for joining me on another amateur radio adventure from Northern New Brunswick!

73, Stuart — VE9CF

localized.title: I Activated This Park… Then POTA Removed It!
localized.description:
I activated this POTA park, made over 300 QSOs, and shortly afterward, POTA removed it from the program! What happened?

Join me for another portable ham radio adventure at the beautiful Village Historique Acadien near Caraquet, New Brunswick, Canada.

This fascinating historical attraction celebrates the rich Acadian heritage of Atlantic Canada, and it turned out to be a fantastic location for amateur radio. With over 300 contacts in the log, the activation was a tremendous success, with plenty of stations eager to make contact with VE9CF.

But there's an unexpected twist to this story!

Shortly after my visit, the Village Historique Acadien was removed from the Parks on the Air (POTA) program.

The removal was carried out by POTA VE9 Mapping Coordinator AB0O, on the same day that 24 other locations were removed during an audit and cleanup of POTA references in New Brunswick and Canada.

Why was this particular historical location removed?

I haven't been given an explanation for its removal, and that's what makes this story particularly interesting. One day it was an eligible POTA location, and shortly afterward, it was gone from the program.

Fortunately, removing a location from POTA doesn't erase the adventure, the contacts, or the wonderful experience of operating portable from such a historic part of New Brunswick.

In this video, you'll experience the activation, hear some of the contacts, and discover why this location has an interesting story beyond the radio contacts themselves.

Thanks for joining me on another amateur radio adventure from Northern New Brunswick!

73, Stuart — VE9CF
